probability, an experimental result, or a substitute for reasoning about the

condition. Infer direction from the record cards first, then judge transfer from
all visible context. Do not invent a numeric similarity judgment or assume that
a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal
hidden chain-of-thought.

claims.claim: All visible human oral-bioavailability measurements in the reference contexts are at or above the F=20% threshold: apixaban ~50%, papaverine 22–29%, alpelisib 50–69%, brepocitinib 75%, vernakalant 58–71% in fasted volunteers, selpercatinib 73%, AZD0837 22–55%, daridorexant 41–62%, and ONO-4641 predicted F=0.71.

L2 records reinforce the high direction: apixaban 34–88% and dog absolute F=88%, alpelisib complete in mice and 58% in rats, daridorexant absolute F=62%, AZD0837 ~22–55%, papaverine relative 54–68%, ONO-4641 monkey F=0.71, and qualitative good oral bioavailability for CPI-0610, brepocitinib, and MK-8628.

The only sub-threshold value, daridorexant rat F=9% at 10 mg/kg, is species-specific and is outweighed by human absolute F=62% and population PK F=0.41; it does not provide affirmative evidence that the query has F<20%.
Fasted-state evidence is supportive: vernakalant absolute F=58–71% in fasted volunteers and apixaban ~50% unaffected by food.
The L5 Caco-2 record for compound 27, a methoxyquinoline basic amine, shows high permeability and no significant efflux, providing weak mechanistic support but no query-specific measurement.
